questions.q: What does the summary say psychedelics can help people do?
a: Step outside ordinary thinking and make new connections
Replace the need for sleep entirely
Improve their memory for factual details
Cure every known physical illness
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the drugs can help with creative solutions and new associations, and may treat PTSD, depression and anxiety.

questions.q: What is the Hedonic Calendar used for?
a: Planning when and how to reach altered states safely
Tracking how many hours you work each week
Scheduling medical appointments for therapy
Recording which foods improve your mood
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes it as a way to choose favorite activities, weigh risk and reward, and schedule them sensibly.

questions.q: What does the summary advise to avoid becoming dependent on ecstasis?
a: Take a month off from the activities that produce it
Limit yourself to one activity per week
Only pursue altered states with a therapist present
Stop all exercise and meditation for a year
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends a month-long break to test whether you can go without those feelings.

questions.q: How does the Hedonic Calendar account for risk?
a: Each activity is assessed with a risk-reward ratio
Risky activities are banned from the calendar
Risk is ignored once the reward is high enough
Only low-cost activities are included
questions.why: Lesson 2 says you rate your favorite activities by weighing the reward against the danger.

questions.q: How might VR help extreme sports enthusiasts?
a: It can deliver a similar thrill with far less danger
It trains them to ignore safety procedures
It replaces the need for physical fitness
It records their performance for sponsors
questions.why: Lesson 3 says indoor VR experiences can match the excitement while reducing real risk, as SEAL Team Six has used.
